jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Manager
jobs.description:
Shape Your World
At Alcoa, you will become an essential part of our purpose: to turn raw potential into real progress. The way we see it, every Alcoan is a work-shaper, team-shaper, idea-shaper & world-shaper.

Alcoa Massena Operations is seeking a Continuous Improvement Manager to lead the advancement of operational excellence and continuous improvement initiatives across the site. This role serves as a key partner to leaders and employees throughout the organization, helping drive sustainable business improvements through the Alcoa Business System (ABS), Lean Manufacturing principles, and structured problem-solving methodologies.

This professional will work cross-functionally with operations, maintenance, support functions, and leadership teams to identify opportunities, improve processes, build internal capability, and deliver measurable business results. This is a highly visible role that combines strategic thinking, change leadership, coaching, and hands-on execution to strengthen performance across the operation.

About the Role
- Lead the deployment and sustainability of Lean Manufacturing systems and continuous improvement initiatives across multiple functional areas, including Production, Maintenance, EHS, Procurement, Human Resources, and other support organizations.

- Partner with leaders and employees to identify opportunities that improve safety, quality, productivity, reliability, and cost performance across the operation.

- Facilitate improvement projects from concept through implementation, ensuring actions are aligned with site objectives and deliver measurable business value.

- Lead initiatives focused on process optimization, cost reduction, operational effectiveness, industrial engineering studies, and business planning activities.

- Develop, coach, and mentor employees and leaders in continuous improvement tools and methodologies, fostering a culture of accountability, ownership, and problem-solving.

- Facilitate structured problem-solving efforts using A3 methodology, standardized work, root cause analysis, and other Lean principles.

- Drive organizational change initiatives that improve customer-supplier connections, eliminate waste, and increase operational efficiency.

- Track, validate, and document business improvements and savings through established reporting systems and performance metrics.

- Support the development of annual operating plans, performance targets, and departmental budgets in partnership with site leadership

- Serve as a trusted advisor and change agent, helping teams adopt and sustain best practices across the organization.

What You Bring
Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree required.

- 4-6+ years of experience leading process improvement, operational excellence, continuous improvement, Lean Manufacturing, or related initiatives.

- Strong understanding of budget development, implementation, and performance management processes.

- Demonstrated experience implementing Lean Manufacturing principles and driving measurable operational improvements.

- Excellent facilitation, coaching, and change management skills.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to translate data into actionable improvements.

- Ability to influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization without direct authority.

- Proven success leading cross-functional teams and driving results in complex environments.

Preferred Qualifications
- Previous leadership experience within a manufacturing, industrial, metals, mining, chemicals, or heavy industrial environment.

- Formal training or certification in Lean, Six Sigma, Operational Excellence, or Continuous Improvement methodologies.

- Experience leading large-scale organizational change initiatives.

- Knowledge of industrial production processes and value stream optimization.

What’s on Offer:
- Competitive compensation packages, including pay-for-performance variable pay as well as recognition and rewards programs

- Flexible spending accounts and generous employer contribution to the HSA

- 401(k), employer match up to 6%, additional employer retirement income contribution (no vesting period), and a non-qualified deferred compensation plan

- 15 vacation days prorated in the 1st year based on hire date

- Alcoa has been chosen as one of America’s Greatest Workplaces 2023 by Newsweek

#LI-TL2

Base Salary: 127,200 - 190,600 USD annually

Total rewards packages listed, including base salary and bonus eligibility, applies to US based applicants only. Actual salaries will vary and will be based on a range of factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, and competencies in conjunction with multiple components of the Employee Total Rewards Package. Alcoa reserves the right to change plans at its discretion.
About the Location
Our Massena facility in New York State, established in 1902, is home to the longest continuously operating smelter in the world. Located on the St. Lawrence River, Massena, NY is the center for commercial, industrial, and manufacturing success in St. Lawrence County. Massena’s caring sense of community, affordable cost of living, and extremely low-cost locally supplied energy, coupled with four public and private universities nearby, make Massena a great place to call home. And within a two hour drive (or less) are cosmopolitan and historic Montreal and Ottawa, Canada to the north, and to the south are the tall, beautiful views of Adirondacks and within it is Lake Placid The Olympic Village.

jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Specialist
jobs.description:
Shape Your World
At Alcoa, you will become an essential part of our purpose: to turn raw potential into real progress. The way we see it, every Alcoan is a work-shaper, team-shaper, idea-shaper & world-shaper.

Shape your world by helping teams turn operational challenges into lasting capability.

As a Continuous Improvement Specialist at Warrick Operations, you will combine hands-on industrial experience, Lean thinking, data insight and strong people skills to support a major step-change effort. You will work closely with leaders, supervisors and employees on the plant floor, coaching teams to solve problems, strengthen daily management and sustain better ways of working.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You will help advance operational excellence across Warrick Operations, with primary focus on the Potroom and Carbon Plant while supporting improvement priorities across the site. This role is not simply about solving problems for others. You will coach, facilitate and build team capability so employees can identify issues, use structured methods and become increasingly autonomous in improving performance. Success requires the ability to connect what you observe in the field with process data, influence change and adapt quickly as business priorities evolve.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

·      Advance the Warrick Lean Plan through the Alcoa Business System framework, using Lean and continuous improvement methods to identify waste, improve flow and strengthen execution.
·      Coach supervisors, operators and cross-functional teams in daily management practices, including shift handoffs, toolbox meetings and Daily Management System meetings.
·      Facilitate Kaizen events, workshops and structured problem-solving sessions that engage the people closest to the work, clarify root causes and build practical action plans.
·      Analyze operational data and observe processes on the plant floor to identify short- and long-term opportunities, translate insights into priorities and monitor progress.
·      Guide improvement initiatives using appropriate structured approaches, including process mapping, value-stream mapping, PDCA and DMAIC principles, while aligning work to site priorities.
·      Lead the people side of change by communicating clearly, influencing stakeholders, adapting to changing priorities and helping teams own and sustain improvements safely.

WHAT YOU BRING

·      A bachelor’s degree in chemical, metallurgical, industrial, manufacturing or process engineering, or in business or a related field combined with relevant heavy-industry experience.
·      Three to five years of experience in an industrial or manufacturing environment, with practical exposure to Lean systems and continuous improvement. Six Sigma certification is welcomed but not required.
·      Demonstrated ability to coach and facilitate rather than simply provide the answer, helping operators and teams build confidence and ownership in problem solving.
·      Strong communication, collaboration and change-management skills, including the confidence to engage stakeholders at different levels and gain support for a shared direction.
·      Strong digital and analytical skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Office tools such as Excel and PowerPoint; experience with Power BI, process software or coding is an advantage.
·      A safety-first, curious and adaptable approach, with the ability to spend meaningful time on the plant floor, compare observations with data and shift priorities in a fast-moving environment.

HOW YOU WILL WORK

You will be part of a small, collaborative continuous improvement team and will partner broadly across Warrick Operations. The strongest candidates will bring credibility in an industrial setting, curiosity about how work is performed, and the ability to help people move through change. You will take accountability, communicate clearly, prioritize and execute, and contribute to a safe, inclusive and collaborative environment.

WHAT WE OFFER

·      Competitive compensation packages, including pay-for-performance variable pay as well as recognition and rewards programs
·      Flexible spending accounts and generous employer contribution to the HSA
·      401(k), employer match up to 6%, additional employer retirement income contribution (no vesting period), and a nonqualified deferred compensation plan
·      Holiday Pay: 10 holidays and one flexible holiday of your choice.
·      Alcoa has been chosen as one of America’s Greatest Workplaces 2023 by Newsweek

Ready to turn ideas into practical improvements and help teams build lasting capability? Join Alcoa and shape your world.

Alcoa “Warrick” based in Newburgh, Indiana just outside of Evansville, IN has been present in the lives of many families in our community for over 60 years. We’ve grown and we’ve matured together. jobs.title: AI Governance Lead
jobs.description:
Shape Your World
At Alcoa, you will become an essential part of our purpose: to turn raw potential into real progress. The way we see it, every Alcoan is a work-shaper, team-shaper, idea-shaper & world-shaper.

At Alcoa, you’re an essential part of our purpose: to turn raw potential into real progress . This is an opportunity for you to bring your wealth of experience to the team and help shape the future of sustainability with world-changing innovations and low-carbon technologies. You have the power to shape things to make them better.

About the role:

At Alcoa, we're not just adopting AI, we're leveraging it to transform how we operate, innovate, and create value across our global business. As our AI Governance Lead, you'll play a pivotal role in ensuring that AI is deployed responsibly, ethically, and securely while helping unlock its full potential across the enterprise.

This is a unique opportunity to build and mature AI governance capabilities at a global industrial leader. You'll work at the intersection of technology, risk, compliance, privacy, legal, and business strategy, helping shape how Alcoa governs AI today and into the future.
If you're passionate about responsible AI, emerging technologies, and influencing enterprise-wide transformation, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do
- Lead and evolve Alcoa’s AI governance framework, including policies, standards, processes, and oversight structures that enable responsible AI adoption.
- Play a key leadership role as a member of the AI Steering Committee and help shape enterprise AI strategy, governance priorities, and decision-making.
- Develop and manage AI intake, inventory, and risk management processes to ensure compliance, transparency, and accountability.
- Partner with Legal, Ethics & Compliance, Data Privacy, Procurement, Cybersecurity, Audit, and business leaders to govern AI technologies and third-party solutions.
- Drive AI awareness, training, and stakeholder engagement programs that promote ethical and responsible AI use across the organization.
- Establish governance metrics, monitoring processes, and executive reporting to measure compliance, risk, adoption, and business value.
- Stay ahead of emerging AI technologies, regulations, and industry trends while helping guide Alcoa’s AI roadmap and future direction.

What you can bring to the role
- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Science, or a related field.
- Experience in AI governance, technology risk management, data governance, compliance, privacy, or a related discipline.
- Strong understanding of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, large language models (LLMs), and associated risks and governance considerations.
- Experience leading cross-functional governance, compliance, risk, or enterprise transformation initiatives.
- Knowledge of AI regulations, data privacy requirements, ethical AI principles, and risk management practices.
- Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and executive presentation skills, with the ability to influence across technical and non-technical audiences.
- Relevant certifications such as CIPP, CIPM, AI governance, data governance, risk management, or related credentials are a plus, as is experience in manufacturing, industrial, or global enterprise environments.

What we offer:
- Competitive compensation packages, including pay-for-performance variable pay, recognition and rewards programs.
- 401(k), employer match up to 6%, additional employer retirement income contribution (no vesting period)
- Healthcare benefits: medical, Rx, dental, vision, flexible spending account, health savings account (generous employer contribution), life and accident insurance
- Work-life balance programs: flexible work scheduling, hybrid/remote working
- Paid time off:  15 vacation days prorated in the 1st year based on hire date, 12 paid holidays, 7 illness days, Care for Family leave up to 40 days, up to 5 bereavement days, maximum of 30 jury duty days, and up to 10 days annual training for military leave

jobs.title: Capital Procurement Site Lead
jobs.description:
Shape Your World
At Alcoa, you will become an essential part of our purpose: to turn raw potential into real progress. The way we see it, every Alcoan is a work-shaper, team-shaper, idea-shaper & world-shaper.

This is your opportunity to shape how Alcoa delivers its capital portfolio at Portland Aluminium Smelter. As the site’s capital procurement lead, you will provide procurement and commercial leadership across capital projects, helping teams make sound sourcing, contracting and supplier decisions that support safe, timely and cost-effective delivery.

About the role
Based at Portland Aluminium Smelter, you will lead capital procurement activities for the site’s portfolio of capital projects. Reporting to the Procurement Manager – Capital in Perth, you will be accountable for translating capital procurement strategy into practical project and site outcomes.

You will oversee the capital procurement pipeline from early project planning through contract close-out. This includes procurement planning, sourcing and market engagement, tendering and evaluation, commercial negotiation, contract formation, supplier performance, variations and claims, governance, risk management and reporting.

Working effectively with appropriate autonomy, you will establish priorities, guide project-specific procurement approaches and provide clear commercial advice to site and project stakeholders. You will balance value, schedule, quality, risk and governance requirements, resolve complex commercial matters and escalate material issues with evidence-based recommendations.

You will also provide day-to-day functional leadership to the site-based capital procurement specialist, including work planning, coaching and quality oversight. Success in the role will rely on your ability to lead through influence and build productive relationships across project, engineering, operations, finance, legal and supplier groups.

In this role, you will:
- Lead capital procurement planning and delivery across Portland Aluminium Smelter’s portfolio of capital projects.
- Develop fit-for-purpose procurement and commercial strategies that support safe, timely, cost-effective and compliant project delivery.
- Lead end-to-end sourcing and contracting for critical and complex capital packages.
- Provide commercial leadership throughout the contract lifecycle, including supplier performance, change management and contract close-out.
- Maintain effective procurement governance and manage commercial, supply, contractor and delivery risks.
- Partner with project, engineering, operational and functional stakeholders to support effective commercial decisions.
- Provide functional leadership, coaching and delivery oversight to the site-based capital procurement specialist.
- Monitor procurement performance, milestones, risks and value outcomes, maintaining alignment with the broader capital procurement team.

What’s on offer
- Attractive remuneration and variable bonus plan.
- Career growth and development opportunities.
- 18 weeks paid parental leave for primary caregivers.
- Paid employee volunteering hours to support our communities.
- Access to the My Alcoa Benefits program, including travel, lifestyle, health and well-being discounts.
- A diverse and inclusive workplace supported by employee inclusion groups.

What you can bring
- A relevant tertiary qualification in procurement, supply chain, business, commerce, engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
- Demonstrated procurement and contract management experience supporting capital projects and complex commercial packages.
- End-to-end experience across procurement planning, sourcing, tendering, negotiation, contracting and supplier performance management.
- Experience in an industrial, resources, manufacturing, heavy engineering or similarly complex project environment is desirable.
- Sound commercial judgement and an understanding of project delivery, contract risk, cost drivers and supply markets.
- The ability to work with autonomy, manage competing priorities and deliver outcomes in a changing environment.
- Effective stakeholder engagement, communication and influencing skills, including the ability to navigate complex commercial matters and raise and explore alternative perspectives.
- Experience providing functional leadership, supported by effective systems capability and a commitment to ethical, safe and accountable decision-making.

Additional information
- Interviews may progress prior to the closing date, although all applications will be considered.
- You will only be contacted if you are shortlisted for an interview, this process can take up to four weeks from the closing date.

Be part of shaping our organisation and join us in building a legacy of excellence for future generations.

jobs.title: Financial Analyst, Finance Leadership Development Rotational Program
jobs.description:
Shape Your World
At Alcoa, you will become an essential part of our purpose: to turn raw potential into real progress. The way we see it, every Alcoan is a work-shaper, team-shaper, idea-shaper & world-shaper.

This is your opportunity to help shape the future of sustainability with world-changing innovations and low-carbon technologies. Become a valued part of the team that’s shaping the future of aluminum, revolutionizing the way the world lives, builds, moves and flies. Be part of it and shape your world.

About the role:

In Alcoa Corporation’s Finance Leadership Development Rotational Program, you’ll have the opportunity to work and learn at one of the world’s most respected companies including being named to the Dow Jones Sustainability Index . Alcoa is a global organization that offers diverse opportunities, exciting challenges and the chance to apply your skills within a world-class finance organization.

In August of each year, the new financial analysts begin their work rotating through four challenging assignments (six months each) in Alcoa’s Finance organization.  The rotations give the analysts first-hand exposure to Alcoa’s business processes and values.  The program also emphasizes professional development with formal and informal feedback, and exposure to executives throughout the rotation.  The rotational assignments are based at Alcoa’s corporate center in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

At the end of the two-year program, the analysts will ideally be placed as an analyst in one of our Resource Units or at one of Alcoa’s production locations.  The program is designed to develop the analysts to take the next step in their finance careers, and ultimately, in their careers as Alcoa business leaders.

Key responsibilities within the four rotational assignments include:

Financial Planning & Analysis
- Develop and analyze financial reporting used by Alcoa’s senior business leaders

- Support business planning and forecasting decisions across Alcoa’s operations

- Analyze performance against key financial metrics

- Partner with plant finance teams to analyze operating results and variances and identify business challenges and opportunities.

Financial Accounting
- Contribute to the monthly close and external financial reporting processes

- Evaluate how emerging accounting requirements affect the business

- Collaborate with team members to develop new or improved accounting policies or procedures

- Communicate the financial implications of accounting and business matters to plant and legal-entity leaders.

Internal Audit
- Evaluate Alcoa’s business processes, internal controls, and management systems

- Assess processes and controls at corporate and operating locations

- Support evaluations of internal controls over financial reporting and compliance with Sarbanes-Oxley requirements

- Identify and communicate process improvement opportunities to business leaders

Treasury/Investor Relations
- Build experience across Treasury activities, which may include cash management, corporate finance, insurance risk management, and digital treasury

- Analyze financial information and contribute to projects supporting liquidity, capital structure, risk management, and investor communications

- Partner with Treasury and Investor Relations professionals on high-priority initiatives

Your education is just beginning!  Beyond challenging work assignments, we’ll help you learn through:
- Corporate and finance-specific training

- Orientations to place your knowledge in the context of Alcoa’s businesses

- Program mentors who will share years of experience and help you to choose the best path for your interests

What you can bring to the role:
- A Bachelor's degree in business – Accounting or Finance majors preferred

- A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher, with a major GPA of 3.2 or higher

- Courses in basic accounting completed with at least a "B" average

- A graduation date of December 2026 or Spring 2027

- Proficient knowledge of Microsoft Office products

- A desire to grow your career within Alcoa

- Strong problem solving and analytical skills

- Excellent communication skills
